blocks.title: Safety reading
blocks.content:
Under the Wound Dressing profile, this construct clears every assessed gate.
Toxicity (ToxinPred3) measures 0.085 against a threshold of 0.380 from the predictor's own cut-off, which is at or below the limit.
Haemolysis (HemoPI2) measures 0.319 against a threshold of 0.550 from the predictor's own cut-off, which is at or below the limit.
Immunogenicity (MHC-I) has no measured value, so it is reported as not assessed rather than as a pass. The pipeline's rule is that an unassessed metric does not eliminate a candidate.
Soft signals, which do not veto: B-cell epitope (soft) 0.280 (threshold 0.151).

blocks.title: Peptide origin and composition
blocks.content:
The peptide is 30 residues, drawn from legacy_mgy_2022 (dataset version 2022-05-01).
Composition: 7 hydrophobic residues (23%), 11 charged (37%), 0 aromatic (0%).
No cysteine residues, so the peptide has no disulfide-mediated structural constraint.
One-dimensional AGGRESCAN gives 0.167, above zero, which indicates some aggregation propensity. The scale is a mean per-residue aggregation score, negative for aggregation-averse sequences.
The direction's functional score is 0.332, produced by AnOxPePred (FRS head).

blocks.title: Linker and assembly
blocks.content:
The linker is GGGGS, 5 residues long, classified as Flexible.
A glycine-serine linker of this kind gives the fused peptide rotational freedom and separates it from the scaffold surface, which matters when the functional epitope would otherwise be masked by the scaffold. The trade-off is that the unstructured segment is more exposed to proteases.
The linker sequence recorded here comes from the sample linker table rather than the curated library, and the construct carries no verified linker choice: the assembly step that produced it picked the first available row.
The construct's stored scaffold binding is `placeholder`. No fused sequence is emitted, because the bound scaffold row holds a marker string rather than a real sequence.

blocks.title: Expression and handling
blocks.content:
Recommended route: Escherichia coli, strain BL21(DE3), pET-28a(+) with an N-terminal His6 tag.
Induction: 0.4 mM IPTG at OD600 0.6–0.8, 25 °C, 6 h. Purification: Ni-NTA, then size exclusion.
This is a recommendation rather than a stored condition: the dataset records no expression host, vector or induction condition for any construct. It is derived from the peptide's predicted properties, its composition, and — where one is bound — the scaffold's class.
Predicted solubility is 0.987 (SoDoPE), at or above the 0.45 planning cut used here, so no solubility tag is added and the standard 25 °C induction is kept. The peptide is 30 residues, short enough that its own folding is not the limiting step; what the yield then depends on is how the carrier behaves.
Predicted thermal stability is 0.560 (TemStaPro). It does not enter the host choice; it bears on storage temperature and on any heating step after purification.
No scaffold is bound to this construct — the stored binding is a placeholder — so the carrier sequence and the construct's total length are unknown, and the host stays at the E. coli default. Binding a library scaffold moves the route to P. pastoris when that scaffold is a recombinant-collagen fragment longer than 600 residues, and to a recA-deficient strain when it is a repeat-rich silk or collagen.
With no fused sequence on the record, a synthetic gene cannot be ordered until that binding is filled in; the route above describes what to do once it is.

blocks.title: Risk register
blocks.content:
Not assessed for this construct: immunogenicity.
Veto gates without a measurement: immunogenicity. These are reported as unassessed rather than as passing.
No fused sequence is available, because the scaffold binding is a placeholder. Any downstream step that needs the full construct sequence cannot proceed on this record.
This construct sits in the bottom channel, which exists as a negative control for comparison rather than as a candidate.
